teaches: Know which move your opponents actually play, not only which one theory calls best — if the principled break is rare at your level, the sidelines around it are where your preparation time belongs.
explains: Know which move your opponents actually play, not only which one theory calls best. The pawn strikes at c5 and the game opens up — the principled continuation, and below master level the one you see least: the early bishop sortie to c4 is far more common and steers into something completely different. Meeting the real break is a small event in a club game.

line: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4
teaches: A capture with two possible recaptures is a fork in the road, not a formality — wait to see which piece takes back before deciding what game you are in.
explains: Black takes, and the pawn on d4 will not survive — but which White piece removes it matters. The knight recapture is the one that leads to the sharp open positions this whole line is played for; taking with the queen instead is a different game, quieter and with the queen already committed. Both are legal here, and Black does not get to choose.

line: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4
teaches: A knight recapturing into the centre is worth more than the material it restores — it takes the squares the opponent's queenside expansion needs. Notice which squares before you plan around them.
explains: The knight takes back in the middle of the board and now covers b5 and e6, the two squares Black's setup cares about most. This is the real open position — the one with a genuine mass of theory behind it, where White has something like ten separate playable schemes from a couple of moves away. Nobody learns all of it at once, and nobody needs to.

line: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6
teaches: When the opponent has many playable setups and you have one useful move, play the useful move — developing with a hit costs nothing and makes them commit first.
explains: The knight comes out and leans on e4. It is the move Black wants in every version of this position, so there is no reason to spend a thought on it: it develops, it asks a question, and it leaves the choice of system to White. The huge branching comes next, and it comes on White's move.
